title: From Fullerton to the Westside: How Khan Saab Became SoCal's First Michelin-Recognised Pakistani Restaurant
excerpt: Chef Imran Ali Mookhi's halal craft kitchen, famous for its zero-proof cocktail bar and Wagyu kebabs, opens its third location on Santa Monica Boulevard this month.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Khan Saab is Southern California's first Michelin-recognized Pakistani restaurant.
  • The restaurant features a unique 100% non-alcoholic cocktail program.
  • Khan Saab's menu blends Pakistani, Indian, and Afghan culinary traditions.
  • The Santa Monica location opens on July 16, marking the brand's third site.
  • Khan Saab celebrates South Asian culture through its dining experience.
Khan Saab's Culinary Journey
2020
Khan Saab opens its first location in Fullerton.
2021
Earns first Michelin Bib Gourmand for a Pakistani restaurant.
2022
Recognized in the MICHELIN guide again.
July 16, 2023
Santa Monica location grand opening.
When Khan Saab Desi Craft Kitchen opens its doors on Santa Monica Boulevard later this month, it will mark the latest chapter in one of Southern California's most improbable culinary success stories — a halal restaurant that earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand, pioneered a zero-proof cocktail programme, and turned Pakistani-Indian cuisine into one of Orange County's most talked-about dining experiences. The Santa Monica location, currently in its soft opening phase with a grand opening set for July 16, is the brand's third, following the flagship in Fullerton and a second in Hawaiian Gardens. Together, they represent the growing ambition of chef-partner Imran Ali Mookhi and business partners Ahmad and Iqbal Hosseini to bring elevated South Asian cuisine to new corners of Los Angeles. ## A Michelin Path Few Have Walked Khan Saab's story begins in 2020, when Mookhi — a Pakistani-born chef who had trained at Tamarind of London in Newport Beach and helmed kitchens at Tantra on Sunset and Tumbi in Santa Monica — opened a 50-seat restaurant on a quiet Fullerton strip dominated by Mexican-American eateries. Within a year, it had earned the first Michelin Bib Gourmand ever awarded to a Pakistani restaurant in Southern California. It has received the recognition every year since. ![Southern California — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f3/Hermosa_Beach_Pier_I_%28262176665%29_%28cropped%29.jpeg) > **"Led by mixologist Ahmad Hosseini, it was the first of its kind in Southern California and only the fourth in the nation when it launched."** "To be recognised in the MICHELIN guide again this year is a true honour," Mookhi said after his latest recognition. "Our success wouldn't be possible without our loyal guests and supportive community." The Michelin Guide's own inspectors have praised Mookhi's "deftness with spices, flavours and in his handling of red meat," singling out dishes like the Khan Biryani, Australian Wagyu, and Tomahawk steak alongside the signature chicken karahi. ## The Zero-Proof Pioneer What sets Khan Saab apart from most Indian restaurants in America — and indeed from most Michelin-recognised establishments — is its 100 per cent non-alcoholic bar programme. Led by mixologist Ahmad Hosseini, it was the first of its kind in Southern California and only the fourth in the nation when it launched. The craft mocktail menu draws on Desi flavours and global techniques. The Tower of Peshawar combines cucumber, basil, and elderflower tonic. The Smoked Negroni is built with Seedlip Spice 94, rose syrup, and Palo Santo bitters, served under a smoke-filled dome. Zero-proof wines, beers, and spirits round out a programme that operates entirely within halal guidelines. For many South Asian diners, particularly those who don't drink for religious or cultural reasons, it removes a barrier that fine dining has long taken for granted. ## The Menu Defies Easy Categorisation ![Santa Monica — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f7/Casa_del_Mar_Santa_Monica_%28cropped%29.jpg)
Innovative Zero-Proof Cocktails
›First 100% non-alcoholic bar in Southern California.
›Craft mocktails inspired by Desi flavors.
›Signature drink: Tower of Peshawar with cucumber and basil.
›Zero-proof wines and spirits available.
The Santa Monica menu, like those at the other locations, pulls from across the Desi diaspora — Pakistani, Indian, and Afghan traditions merge with modern steakhouse sensibilities. Fried butter chicken shares menu space with pomegranate-braised brisket. Seekh kebabs sit alongside New York strip with grilled vegetables. Street food gets particular attention: bhel puri, pani puri, and chaat appear alongside more refined preparations. The menu clearly flags dairy-free, gluten-free, vegan, and allergen-containing items — a level of transparency unusual in South Asian restaurants. ## What It Means for the Diaspora For the estimated 600,000 Pakistani Americans and four million Indian Americans in the United States, Khan Saab represents something larger than a restaurant expansion. It is proof that South Asian cuisine can command Michelin-level attention without compromising on halal principles, cultural identity, or the communal warmth that defines Desi hospitality. The Santa Monica location sits at 115 Santa Monica Boulevard, with weekday hours from 4 PM to 10:30 PM and weekend hours starting at 2 PM. Reservations are available through OpenTable.
A Menu of Cultural Fusion
›Menu combines Pakistani, Indian, and Afghan dishes.
›Features fried butter chicken and pomegranate-braised brisket.
›Street food options like bhel puri and pani puri.
›Transparency with allergen and dietary information.
"This isn't just about food," Mookhi has said. "It's about celebrating our culture." For a generation of diaspora diners who grew up toggling between their parents' kitchens and mainstream American restaurants, that celebration has been a long time coming.
